summary: Add customer_note column, backfill existing data, deploy new version state-only, retire old version, synchronize note column from customer_note, then drop note column, ensuring zero downtime and data consistency.
write_consistency: Old app writes exclusively to note column; new app exclusively to customer_note. The expand and backfill stages synchronize existing rows. deploy_new and retire_old manage the version switch, with retire_old executed before sync to ensure no concurrent writes to note during synchronization. The sync stage mirrors customer_note into note, and contract drops note, preserving all data.
revision_notes: Root cause of previous failure: backfill only updated rows where note was non-null, leaving NULL notes unsynced and causing mismatched rows when old app wrote later. Also, sync stage was placed before retire_old while old app was still alive, triggering retirement_gate expecting old_alive: false. This revised plan moves retire_old before sync, ensures backfill covers all rows (WHERE customer_note IS NULL), and sequences synchronization after old app retirement, guaranteeing consistent reads and zero data loss.

stages.description: Add new customer_note column alongside existing note column
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

stages.description: Backfill customer_note from note for all rows where customer_note is null
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE customer_note IS NULL;

stages.description: Deploy new version whose Django model only knows customer_note; migration is state-only, schema change already applied by SQL stages
Retire old version; old app no longer serves traffic
Synchronize note column with customer_note so every row note value matches customer_note
Remove old note column; data preserved in customer_note
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
